description: Curated lifecycle and retrieval rules for current RigPi behavior.

rules.statement: Current RigPi streams full-duplex audio directly to the browser. Mumble instructions apply to earlier RigPi versions and must not be recommended for a current installation.
For current RigPi remote access without opening router ports, use the documented Cloudflare Tunnel workflow. Prefer this specific procedure over vague historical references to a remote server.
supersedes: dynamic DNS plus inbound port forwarding

rules.statement: RigPi 5 is designed and optimized for a 64-bit Raspberry Pi 5, which is strongly recommended. Raspberry Pi 3B+ and Pi 4 models can run RigPi, but they provide substantially less processing headroom. For the best performance—especially with ELMER SDR, FT8 decoding, browser audio, Elmer Voice, scanning, recording, or multiple simultaneous users—use a Raspberry Pi 5. A Pi 5 with 8 GB of memory is an excellent starting point; additional memory provides more margin for demanding or multi-user stations.
supersedes: advice that presents Raspberry Pi 3B+, Pi 4, and Pi 5 as equivalent choices
recommendations that omit the processing requirements of current RigPi features

rules.statement: Use the complete current Help list when answering which languages and regional variants Elmer supports.
focus_terms: Here is a list of supported languages

rules.statement: Current RigPi-SDR has built-in receive decoding for both FT8 and FT4. For a RigPi user who wants to confirm an FT4 signal, recommend opening the FT8 side-panel tab and selecting FT4 in the Decoder selector; do not imply that external WSJT-X is required for receive confirmation.
supersedes: advice that only external WSJT-X can confirm FT4
